2609.11569.title: Enabling Knowledge Graph Understanding at Scale with the EXplore Your Graphs ENgine (EXYGEN)
2609.11569.paper_summary: We present EXYGEN (EXplore Your Graphs ENgine), a framework for knowledge graph (KG) understanding that enables conversational access to KGs at scale. We address two questions in sequence. First, how effectively can LLMs perform text-to-SPARQL generation given only automatically derived structured metadata and small graph samples, rather than task-specific fine-tuning? We integrate VoID descriptions and ShEx schemas into a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline and ablate KG-derived context on the SciQA benchmark. Our best configuration -- combining ShEx schemas, retrieved triples, and example question-query pairs -- reaches an exact match of 0.419 on execution results without any LLM fine-tuning. We further find that lexical metrics such as F1 poorly predict query correctness, and that larger general-purpose LLMs can outperform smaller code-specialized ones once given sufficient context. Second, we ask how to generate the structured metadata that this method relies on from very large KGs, where KG metadata generation becomes computationally intractable. We introduce a predicate-coverage-aware parallel graph sampling strategy that preserves structural diversity while remaining computationally tractable. On OpenCitations Meta and GESIS, it retains high predicate coverage with minimal triple loss and reduces runtime by over 80x; on ORKG, sampling is not just faster but the only tractable path to obtain complete metadata. Together, these results show that structured schema context and lightweight prompting can substantially reduce reliance on fine-tuning for scalable conversational access to KGs, though closing the remaining gap to fully fine-tuned approaches will likely require reducing dependence on curated question-query exemplars -- whether through synthetic generation or an execution-feedback-driven approach -- and validating these findings beyond a single benchmark.
2609.11569.paper_summary_zh: 我們提出了 EXYGEN（EXplore Your Graphs ENgine），這是一個用於知識圖譜（KG）理解的框架，能夠實現對 KG 的大規模對話訪問。我們依次解決兩個問題。首先，當僅使用自動生成的結構化元數據和小型圖樣本，而不是針對特定任務的微調時，LLM 在文本到 SPARQL 生成方面的表現有多有效？我們將 VoID 描述和 ShEx 架構整合到檢索增強生成（RAG）管道中，並在 SciQA 基準上進行 KG 衍生上下文的消融。我們的最佳配置——結合 ShEx 架構、檢索的三元組和示例問題-查詢對——在執行結果上達到了 0.419 的精確匹配，且不需要任何 LLM 微調。我們進一步發現，像 F1 這樣的詞彙指標對查詢正確性預測不佳，並且一旦給予足夠的上下文，更大的通用 LLM 可以超越較小的專門化代碼模型。其次，我們詢問如何從非常大的 KG 生成這種方法所依賴的結構化元數據，因為 KG 元數據生成變得計算上不可行。我們引入了一種考慮謂詞覆蓋的並行圖採樣策略，該策略在保持結構多樣性的同時仍然計算上可行。在 OpenCitations Meta 和 GESIS 上，它保持了高謂詞覆蓋率，並且三元組損失最小，運行時間減少超過 80 倍；在 ORKG 上，採樣不僅更快，而且是獲得完整元數據的唯一可行途徑。總體而言，這些結果表明，結構化架構上下文和輕量級提示可以顯著減少對微調的依賴，以實現可擴展的對話訪問 KG，儘管縮小與完全微調方法之間的剩餘差距可能需要減少對策劃問題-查詢示例的依賴——無論是通過合成生成還是執行反饋驅動的方法——並在單一基準之外驗證這些發現。
